performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body:
Hi @usualoma Thanks for #5536! I merged it. I found one more problem #5539. If a handler calls `text()` first and then `formData()`, a binary file in the multipart body is broken. This is because we rebuild the bytes from the text. The same thing happens with `application/octet-stream` or a non-UTF-8 charset. Then, how about adding a change like this: ```diff diff --git a/src/request.ts b/src/request.ts index d09fb244..6af24060 100644 --- a/src/request.ts +++ b/src/request.ts @@ -26,6 +26,9 @@ type Body = { } type BodyCache = Partial> +const utf8TextRegex = + /^(?:text\/|application\/(?:[\w.-]+\+)?json|application\/x-www-form-urlencoded)(?!.*charset=(?!utf-?8\b))/i + type OptionalRequestInitProperties = 'window' | 'priority' type RequiredRequestInit = Required> & { [Key in OptionalRequestInitProperties]?: RequestInit[Key] @@ -224,14 +227,11 @@ export class HonoRequest

{ // and a header read afterwards would not match the serialized bytes const contentType = raw.headers.get('content-type') if (key === 'text') { - const text = (bodyCache.text ??= ( - bodyCache.arrayBuffer - ? (bodyCache.arrayBuffer as unknown as Promise).then((buffer) => - new TextDecoder().decode(buffer) - ) - : raw.text() - ) as never) as unknown as Promise - return text as Promise + return (bodyCache.text ??= ( + !bodyCache.arrayBuffer && contentType && utf8TextRegex.test(contentType) + ? raw.text() + : this.#cachedBody('arrayBuffer').then((buffer) => new TextDecoder().decode(buffer)) + ) as never) as unknown as Promise } const bytes = (bodyCache.arrayBuffer ??= ( bodyCache.text ``` The idea is that we use the text as the source only when the body is UTF-8 text. For everything else, we read the bytes first. But using the regex will introduce some performance degradation.
